neet_che_u03_t00_1.working: In BF3, boron has only 6 valence electrons (3 bond pairs), so its octet is incomplete. The central atoms in NH3, CH4 and H2O all complete their octets.

neet_che_u03_t00_2.working: Formal charge on O = 6 - 2 (one lone pair) - 3 (half of 6 bonding electrons) = +1.

neet_che_u03_t00_3.working: NO has 11 valence electrons and NO2 has 17, so both are odd-electron molecules. CO, SO2 and N2O all have even electron counts.

neet_che_u03_t00_4.working: A is false because Xe forms compounds such as XeF2, XeF4 and XeO3. R is true: noble gases have a stable octet (duplet for He).

neet_che_u03_t00_5.working: Statement I is incorrect: formal charge is a bookkeeping device, not the actual charge on the atom. Statement II is correct: I in IF7 has 7 bond pairs, i.e. 14 electrons, an expanded octet.
